name: St Mark's biofeedback trial
question: In patients with fecal incontinence, do sphincter exercise instruction or biofeedback improve outcomes beyond standard advice?

design.blinding: Patients and therapists unblinded; repeat anorectal physiologist blinded

arms.label: hospital biofeedback plus home electromyogram biofeedback

design.population: 171 adults referred for fecal incontinence of any frequency or severity at a specialist colorectal hospital.
design.locator: Full text, Methods, pp 1321-1322; Table 2, p 1323

verdictNote: Neither primary rating favored biofeedback; the home-device arm rated less improvement.
takeaway: In 171 patients with fecal incontinence, advice, added sphincter exercises, hospital pressure biofeedback, and hospital plus home electromyogram biofeedback were compared. Global ratings of worse, same, improved, or cured did not differ (P=0.54); the home-device arm rated less change despite a four-group difference (P=0.048).

reports.label: Randomized report
reports.citation: Norton C, Chelvanayagam S, Wilson-Barnett J, et al. Randomized controlled trial of biofeedback for fecal incontinence. *Gastroenterology.* 2003;125(5):1320-1329. doi:10.1016/j.gastro.2003.09.039
reports.followUp: At treatment completion; improvements largely maintained 1 year after treatment
reports.followUpLocator: Full text, Results at 1-Year Follow-up, p 1326

results.endpoint: Patient-rated global outcome (worse, same, improved, or cured)
results.measure: Global rating of worse, same, improved, or cured after treatment; noncompleters counted as unchanged (ITT)
results.note: Four-group Fisher exact test P=0.54; percentages for advice and hospital pressure feedback are reported in the paper's abstract.
results.locator: Full text, Outcome Measures, p 1321; Patient Assessment of Outcome, p 1324; abstract, p 1320

results.measure: Median change on -5 to +5 scale after treatment; noncompleters counted as zero (ITT)
results.note: Kruskal-Wallis four-group difference was driven by poorer outcome in the home-device arm, opposite the expected superiority direction.
results.locator: Full text, Outcome Measures, p 1321; Patient Assessment of Outcome and Figure 3, p 1324

results.measure: Pooled median episodes per week before and after treatment among available paired diaries
results.note: Median accidents decreased from 2 to 0 per week (P < 0.001); 39% of post-treatment diaries were missing. Post-treatment medians were 1, 0, 0, and 0 for advice, exercise, hospital, and home-device groups; between-group P=0.51.
results.locator: Full text, Comparison of All Trial Patients Before and After Treatment, p 1325; Table 3, p 1325

results.measure: Pooled median continence score before and after treatment; worst score 20
results.note: In the pooled paired analysis, the median score decreased from 15 to 13 (P ≤ 0.001); post-treatment medians were 13, 11, 13, and 14 for advice, exercise, hospital, and home-device groups; between-group P=0.54. The paper's abstract instead gives 11 to 8.
results.locator: Full text, Comparison of All Trial Patients Before and After Treatment and Table 3, p 1325; abstract, p 1320

results.measure: Proportion of 1-year questionnaire respondents reporting improved bowel control
results.note: 74% of respondents reported improvement; 106/160 eligible patients replied (66%), including 95 with paired immediate and 1-year responses. No between-group difference was detected.
results.locator: Full text, Results at 1-Year Follow-up, p 1326

delivery.label: Biofeedback modalities

values.home: Hospital biofeedback plus a 20-minute daily home electromyogram biofeedback device

delivery.note: All groups received nurse-led assessment, education, lifestyle and bowel advice, emotional support, and an urge-resistance program; hospital feedback displayed external sphincter contraction pressure, while the home unit used an intra-anal electromyogram electrode and illuminated muscle-activity lights.
delivery.locator: Full text, Table 1 and Groups 1-4, pp 1321-1322

delivery.label: Sphincter exercise dose
delivery.value: At least 50 maximal sustained and 50 fast-twitch contractions daily in groups 2-4
delivery.locator: Full text, Group 2 and Table 1, p 1321

delivery.label: Treatment sessions and completion
delivery.value: Up to nine 40-60-minute sessions over 3-6 months; median five sessions (range 1-9); 140/171 (82%) completed protocol and outcome questionnaires
delivery.locator: Full text, Group 1, p 1321; Patients Completing Study Protocol, p 1323; Table 3, p 1325

delivery.label: Surgery for persistent fecal incontinence
delivery.value: Nine patients had surgery before the 1-year questionnaire follow-up
delivery.locator: Full text, Results at 1-Year Follow-up, p 1326
